aspose.3d foss for python reads and writes obj, stl, gltf, and collada files, and provides classes for mesh, geometry, curve, and shading manipulation.

- `nurbscurve.evaluate()` and `nurbssurface.to_mesh()` raise `notimplementederror` — nurbs curves and surfaces can be configured but not sampled or converted to a `mesh`, and `pointcloud.from_geometry()` and `pointcloud.from_geometry_with_density()` raise `notimplementederror`, and `axissystem` raises `notimplementederror` on every method including construction.

these limitations don't apply to [full-featured aspose.3d for python — enterprise edition](https://products.aspose.com/3d/python-net/). it adds broader proprietary-format support (pdf, ply, usd, and more), rendering, and advanced mesh operations that this foss build leaves unimplemented.

aspose.3d foss for python requires python 3.7 or later and supports versions 3.7 through 3.12 on windows, macos, and linux with no native dependencies. the test suite resides in the tests/ directory and covers obj, stl, gltf, collada, and 3mf import/export, polygon triangulation, and format-detection behavior. build and test commands for autonomous coding tools are documented in `agents.md`.
